en: Chapter Thirty: The Ritual Manual of the Great Majestic Power of the Mantra of the Wrathful King Yamāntaka, from the Mahāyāna Vaipulya Mañjuśrī-bodhisattva Avataṃsaka Root Teaching.
At that time, the Great Yakṣa General Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat within that assembly,
bared his right shoulder, and placed his right knee upon the ground.
Joining his palms in reverent salutation to the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has not yet extensively explained the wrathful king Yamāntaka."
I observe sentient beings in the future,
at a time of great terror during the final dharma period, when the Buddha's teachings have vanished following the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa.
There are no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas who remain apart from the Buddha-fields,
because they protect and uphold the True Dharma, so that the Dharma-realm may endure for a long time,
and in order to subdue all unruly, rebellious, and false kings.
Regarding those who do not benefit the Three Jewels,
the Bodhisattva, through skillful means, uses these inconceivable dharmas to punish,
subdue, and bring them to fulfillment.
Because they mature [beings] through the inconceivable Dharma so that they may leave the evil destinies,
they cause those who uphold the Buddha-Dharma to abide by the teachings of the Dharma at a time when the Buddha-Dharma is fading away.
The recitation of the wrathful king Yamāntaka shall result in certain accomplishment for all,
except for those sentient beings who do not benefit the Buddha’s teachings, as well as rebellious and false kings;
[this applies] to those sentient beings who do not benefit the Buddha’s teachings.
"This application is for Yamāntaka, the Wrathful King, and not for others.
At that time, the World-Honored One silently entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the sport of supernatural powers.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī also remained in silent stillness.
The entire assembly shook in six ways,
and the hosts of devas were all struck with alarm and terror.
All the devas, nāgas, and asura kings,
as well as the mātṛkā goddesses, all the planetary deities, and the hosts of gods and humans—
these were all shaken and their hearts gave rise to suffering and distress.
The malevolent piśācas and those who are violent and cruel all take refuge in the teaching of the Dharma King and the Great Majestic Power of the Secret Lord Yakṣa Vajrapāṇi,
and they take refuge in the mantra-samaya of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
They all spoke thus: "Mañjuśrī, we pray that you will look upon us with compassion and grant us protection;
we are being scorched by this wrathful mantra."
We were all tormented by suffering and fell to the ground in a swoon.
At that time, Mahātejas, in the form of the youth Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta, spoke these words:
O gods and others, do not fear; neither yakṣas, rākṣasas,
nor the hosts of asuras, nor humans, non-humans, ghosts, or spirits can transgress the samaya that I have proclaimed.
And all you bhūtas and others, arouse hearts of compassion;
together contemplate the Perfectly Enlightened One, the Dharma King, the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings, the Lion of the Śākyas, the Benevolent King. That Buddha has spoken this mantra.
Buddhoṣṇīṣa, Buddhalocanā, and others; the supreme high crown of the gathered wheel-light within the triple world;
the most excellent Uṣṇīṣa-mantra; Padmapāṇi Avalokiteśvara; the holy Lord Avalokiteśvara.
Bikūṭī and Tārā, the Illustrious Consorts Yaśodharā and Pāṇḍaravāsinī,
as well as the Great White One; Hayagrīva, the Lord of Terrific Majesty at the time of the *yālavartī*, and the Vidyārāja of the Lotus Family.
The supreme emanation of the Buddha, the sovereign of the one-syllable Cakravartin mantra,
the one to be contemplated, the God among Gods,
the luminous Lord of Great Ferocity, the Great Wrathful Yamāntaka.
One should also call to mind Avalokiteśvara, who, out of compassion arising from his heart,
proclaimed [this] because of the former Buddhas; it was spoken by Tārā for the sake of saving sentient beings,
while he dwelt in the samādhi of compassion.
The Noble One manifests in female form;
this is the bodhisattva practicing the conduct of awakening.
Throughout the thousands of worlds and further across countless realms, they travel through all manner of hardships.
Rescuing all sentient beings, he subdues them by assuming the form of a woman of exquisite beauty;
he establishes them in the vehicle of enlightenment and teaches for the sake of all bodhisattvas— one should call to mind Vajrapāṇi.
The Mantra King of Diligent Valor, the Holder of the Ma-mok-ke clan,
the one worthy of offerings in the three realms, the one renowned as the Vajra Fist of the Linked Chain Mikhara,
the Wrathful One with the Excellent Moon Mark.
With a terrifying form like a blue staff, such a host of messengers is named the Wrathful Celestial Teacher. He is the most excellent of the Vajra family;
if one recollects him, he provides protection. He is the fragrant elephant within the world.
The Bodhisattva of Great Majestic Power, the eldest son of the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the sublime and majestic Samantabhadra—
if one recollects him at this time, one will be far removed from all terrors.
Furthermore, one should constantly keep in mind the Great Sovereign Yakṣa King Ratnabhadra,
the most supreme; may the assemblies of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas all be free from every fear— if one makes offerings to them.
They immediately obtain great protection; the gods of the Vast Fruit and the Heaven of Merit-Birth,
as well as those of the Form and Formless Realms, who have abandoned desire and possess great majesty,
and those who make offerings to the Triple Gem with pure faith in the Buddha’s teaching.
All those are non-existent; that which is neither friend nor foe, yet inspires fear, is called the Samaya.
This wrathful one, supreme among all mantras, is difficult to overcome; thus it was spoken by Yamāntaka.
Universally protecting all sentient beings, all the hosts of devas and humans were filled with joy; each abiding in their original vows,
the sons of the Buddha all offered praise upon hearing these words of contempt.
The wrathful lord of yakṣas caused countless thousands of worlds to tremble at that time;
O sons of the Buddha, why did you first proclaim this wrathful king as being of no benefit?
The King of Wrath, with majestic power, tamed the violent sentient beings;
standing amidst the great assembly, he spoke aloud to Vajrapāṇi, who,
having received his command, cast down the vajra-pestle.
Then that one of great majesty, the Honored One of wondrous voice and wisdom, in the form of a youth, mocked him and spoke these words:
"Do not act wickedly, O Great Yakṣa; [you are no match for] the majesty of Vajrapāṇi."
This noble Wrathful King whom I have taught— I now bestow this upon you; explain it at will and in detail.
How could you ever fully describe the majestic power of this Wrathful King?
This is what you are entrusted to uphold; as it manifests within the body, summon them all to assemble.
The Heart Mantra then asks and answers, unable to manifest transformations—the wrathful Aivisha.
Listen as you proclaim this in detail: abandoning the samaya,
neglecting ritual bathing, indulging in sleep, following after sensual desires,
anointing with oil, craving perfumes and ornaments, and harboring a mind of constant anger.
Abandoning the supreme mantras, lacking pure faith in the Buddha’s teachings and harboring doubts regarding the True Dharma; engaging in evil conduct,
lacking pure faith in the sublime Dharma and the Sangha Jewel, and slandering with a distracted and agitated mind.
Polluting the Three Jewels, they do not abide within the realm of purity;
failing to maintain the secrecy of the mantra teachings, they are perpetually defiled and devoid of compassion.
Within their celestial abodes, temples, and places of practice, they engage in defiled conduct.
All such types as these who have violated the samaya vows of the wrathful deities—
whether they fail to know the mudrās and mantras or even slightly neglect their conduct— all shall be punished by the wrathful ones.
In all places among humans, one cannot escape heedlessness;
when the mind is stained by heedlessness, the Wrathful King finds an opportunity to violate the samaya. Thus it is for fools in every situation.
Following after heedlessness, the practitioner of mantras should abandon desire for liberation;
just as the Wrathful Kings can coerce Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, Mañjuśrī acts with a heart of compassion.
Having spoken these words concerning the inconceivable conduct of all Buddhas and the great majesty of the Bodhisattvas,
he remained silent and composed. At that time, the auspicious and greatly majestic Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva—
Having received this seal of approval, he leaped for joy;
he then reached out his hand and grasped the vajra.
